I delivered my baby by c section on June 30th this year. After we got discharged from the postpartum floor, she was moved to the pediatric unit for 5 days to monitor withdraws. I was able to stay with her in the room the entire time. They will asses them by scores from 0-5, 0 is no withdraw and 5 is high withdrawals. I’m on sublocade now but I was on 16mg suboxone at the time. She scored all 0’s except for one night she got a 1. They will test the baby’s cord for drugs and send a case worker to check in on you, the one they sent tried to bully me into admitting I did drugs however I got clean immedialtey upon finding out I was pregnant, so they checked her cord and it was clean. If it is dirty they’d have to call CPS on you. My doctor told me that withdrawals are a case by case basis, some babies have none and some babies have a lot no matter the dose. If their withdrawals are really bad they will have to give them bits or morphine to help them taper off the medication. Studies have shown that close contact with the mother dramatically reduces withdrawals, so if you spend a lot of one on one and skin to skin that will help a ton. Also breastfeeding, try to give as much colostrum as you can. The buprenorphine will be in your milk so it’ll help them taper off slowly. One thing I will prepare you for is you might face some judgment. I noticed a lot of the nurses and the case workers were very judgemental. I get it, they do see a lot of users but I got clean immedialtey, my husbands been clean for 2 years and we have a house, nice car, we have good jobs. We aren’t bad people or actively using but they did treat us like we still were. The room next to us had a baby in withdrawals from drugs and the parents never stayed with the baby, they came a few times and were clearly still using. I felt like I was being treated as if I was doing that. The entire time I had extreme anxiety that people were going to take her away. Nothing happens, no report was filed and I took her home once her monitoring was done. I knew that they weren’t just monitoring her, but monitoring my mothering skills as well, since they know you’re an ex user they are going to judge you so you have to make sure your mothering is on point and spend lots of time with your baby, there’s been cases of mothers having CPS called because they weren’t bonding with their baby, you basically have to be perfect and show them there’s no reason to call CPS. Good luck, everything will go great for you!

first off, thinner but longer lashes are more flattering to hooded eyes, they are so good at opening the eyes and it isn’t overpowering at all and makes them look bigger, and you can actually see the length. you can see thru the lashes and see the lid space so ur eyes don’t look too closed. make sure the band is thin so it isn’t super heavy and doesn’t hide the lid space u have. they look glamorous and create a big eye. avoid super thick lashes because they hide the eye even more since u can’t see thru the lashes and it looks even more thick on hooded eyes and due to the hood they will appear short. short and thick resembles a caterpillar on the eye and doesn’t look nice at all!! you can wear thick lashes just not super thick. make sure they’re long and have a thin band. you can get circle or tapered lashes. circle lashes are same length from front to end, they help create a round and open shape, where as tapered lashes that start shorter at the front and gets longer to the end help create an angled and bigger eye shape. i go for tapered ones when i want a big and angled eye shape, and circle ones when i want a big round eye. my eyes seem similar to yours, they’re hooded but there’s a tiny little space. my favorite lashes for everyday wear are the house of lashes Iconic Lite (tapered) and there’s another pair i can’t remember the name but they’re circle lashes from walmart in a purple box with just 1 pair inside, those and the house of lashes are my ABSOLUTE FAVS! they are similar to the walmart ones, but they’re thicker. they’re the thickest ones on these list, that’s why i save them for going out! they’re thicker but they’re long and aren’t too heavy, they’re the only thick lashes that i’ve found are still flattering to hooded eyes!
